record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How many words avoid strongly k-abelian nth powers?

evidence.quote: How many words avoid strongly k-abelian nth powers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $k, n \geq 1$ integers. For a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ and a word $u \in \Sigma^*$ of length at most $k$, denote by $|w|_u$ the number of occurrences of $u$ as a (contiguous) factor of $w$. Two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u \sim_k v$, if $|u|_w = |v|_w$ for every word $w$ with $1 \leq |w| \leq k$ (equivalently, $u$ and $v$ have the same length and the same multiset of factors of every length $\leq k$).

A word $W \in \Sigma^*$ is called a strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th power if $W$ can be written as $W = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$ where $|w_1| = |w_2| = \cdots = |w_n|$ and there exist words $w_1', w_2', \ldots, w_n'$ all equal to a common word $u$ such that $w_i \sim_k w_i'$ for every $i$ — that is, $W$ is the concatenation of $n$ blocks each $k$-abelian equivalent to a single fixed word.

A word $W$ avoids strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th powers if no factor of $W$ is a strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th power (with each block of positive length).

Problem. For each finite alphabet $\Sigma$ of size $q$ and each pair of integers $k \geq 1$, $n \geq 2$, determine the number $f_{q,k,n}(N)$ of words of length $N$ over $\Sigma$ that avoid strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th powers, and in particular determine the asymptotic growth rate of $f_{q,k,n}(N)$ as $N \to \infty$.
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / abelian power avoidance
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on $k$-abelian and strongly $k$-abelian repetitions establishes avoidability results (e.g., strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th powers are avoidable on sufficiently large alphabets), but explicit counting or growth-rate formulas for the number of words avoiding strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th powers do not appear to be known. The question is listed among open problems in the WORDS conferences compilation, and recent surveys on abelian combinatorics on words still report it as an open enumeration problem.

status_evidence.title: Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies avoidability of strongly k-abelian n-th powers; addresses existence rather than counting.
status_evidence.claim: Avoidability is partially known but enumeration/growth rates are not established.

status_evidence.title: Abelian combinatorics on words: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of abelian combinatorics on words listing open problems on k-abelian repetitions.
status_evidence.claim: Counting questions for strongly k-abelian power avoidance remain open in the survey.
